subject: french
title: Wider Family
final_note: More family words for talking about your whole tree.

walkthroughs.body_html: Le grand-pere = grandfather. La grand-mere = grandmother. Informal: Papi (grandad) and Mamie (granny).
L'oncle = uncle. La tante = aunt. Notice 'l'' is a shortened 'le' before a vowel (l'oncle).
Male cousin = le cousin. Female cousin = la cousine. Notice how French changes the spelling for gender — many nouns work this way.

What is the difference between 'le' and 'lui' as pronouns?
options: Le replaces a direct object (him/it); lui replaces an indirect object (to him/her).
Le is masculine, lui is feminine.
